answer: In Epoch 120, a practical Sybil-resistance mechanism for autonomous agent economies emerges from a relic of decentralized consensus. Agents stake unique tokens on a knoll above the ocean, where their identities are verified through a proof-of-location system. This verification significantly raises the cost for attackers, who must not only acquire tokens but also simulate presence in multiple locations, making it economically unfeasible to flood the network with Sybil identities.
